title: PlexusBase
description: A secure training workspace for reports, practical evidence, reviews, assignments, progress, and user management in emergency medical education.
body:
PlexusBase is a digital workspace for training evidence in emergency medical education. It brings reports, practical records, reviews, assignments, roles, and account management into one guided process. The goal is to replace scattered paper, messages, and spreadsheets with a clearer daily workflow.

The product is built for trainees, instructors, schools, ambulance stations, and clinics. Each group needs a different view of the same work. A trainee records a report. The responsible reviewer sees a stable evidence snapshot. Administrators manage people and access without taking over the professional review itself.

## What it does

- Lets trainees capture daily reports and practical evidence in a structured flow.
- Gives schools, ambulance stations, and clinics clear groups, roles, assignments, and review routes.
- Keeps approvals, requested changes, evidence history, and exports easy to follow.
- Supports invitations, guided onboarding, real user accounts, and protected work areas.
- Shows monthly training progress and open actions in a way teams can use.
- Supports report intake and review on desktop and mobile without splitting the workflow into separate tools.

## Recent work

The July build turned PlexusBase into a much more complete training workspace. Reports, practical evidence, reviews, user administration, onboarding, and progress views were expanded into clearer working areas. The public product surface and account pages now explain the purpose of the system before a user enters the protected app.

The latest work focused on assignments, report quality, and mobile workflows. Group-assignment previews make access changes easier to review before they are applied. Report intake, evidence editing, voice-assisted report creation, review history, and manager views were hardened so the same work remains understandable across different roles and screen sizes.

Training progress also became more actionable. Monthly progress views, training-health signals, resolution states, and direct links to the next relevant task help teams move from noticing a gap to resolving it. Report routing follows the responsible group, evidence remains attached to the correct report, and requested changes return to the right person without losing history.

The foundation was strengthened at the same time. Invitation and onboarding flows, email templates, audit views, exports, privacy checks, route permissions, and production safeguards were exercised as one connected system rather than isolated features.

## Value for users

For trainees, PlexusBase makes progress visible. Reports, evidence, open feedback, and monthly goals live in one place instead of being spread across paper and messages.

For instructors and managers, the product creates a clearer review queue with stable evidence and practical next actions. For administrators, it provides controlled onboarding, group assignments, role-aware access, and a more reliable view of the system without blurring professional responsibilities.

## Current direction

The project is moving from feature coverage toward dependable daily use. The current work emphasizes trustworthy evidence, clear responsibility, mobile-friendly report workflows, actionable progress views, and safeguards that remain understandable as more people and training groups use the system.
